correctness.rationale: The centered k-subset orbit has unit vectors and exact second moment p2/(n-1). Expanding distinct-index correlations for exchangeable signs yields A p2²+B p4 with B=16k(n-k)[n²+n−6k(n-k)]/[n(n−1)(n−2)(n−3)]. Two explicit mean-zero vectors for every n≥4 have different p4/p2² and force B=0. Under that equation A matches the sphere fourth moment 3p2²/[(n−1)(n+1)]. Polarization plus antipodal odd moments proves exactness through degree five, including multiplicity when k=n/2. Algebraic Pell transformation gives all j≥2. CHECK.py contains 425 passing exact-rational identities and direct subset enumerations; finite tests do not supply the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The known 56-point tight fifth-design case and the general harmonic-moment criterion are credited. The distinguishable assessed statement is the all-integer necessity and sufficiency for antipodal centered Johnson orbits, including infinitely many Pell cases. No equivalent classification was found in searches of indexed findings, accessible historical claims, primary slice-harmonic results and other general spherical-design constructions. The full 1977 foundational article, the 2009 survey, and the full Reznick article remain incompletely inspected, leaving genuine but not currently decisive coverage risk.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalence may be implicit in full Delsarte–Goethals–Seidel (1977) or Bannai–Bannai (2009); full texts were unavailable despite bounded open-access attempts and an unsuccessful institutional access attempt.
Reznick (1995) was inspected at abstract level only, and may contain a related orbit construction not evident from its abstract.
General Johnson-scheme harmonic formulas can potentially imply the criterion after specialization, which could weaken its standalone novelty.
The first 56-point tight spherical fifth-design case is known and is not independently novel.

value.rationale: This is a natural equal-weight spherical cubature question for an entire irreducible permutation orbit: it determines exactly when a canonical antipodal hypersimplex configuration reproduces every degree≤5 spherical polynomial. The integer condition has infinitely many nontrivial Pell solutions, including the new-parameter 592020-point configuration at n=27 and unbounded higher dimensions. The same argument excludes every off-equation orbit in this family and produces a directly implementable cubature rule, rather than an isolated finite numerical invariant. It makes no minimality or priority claim and does not assert higher cubature strength.
